pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all rows are 0 and the CHECK rejects 2.
test/starred.test.js 'AC-2' asserts the exact list with ★ only on the starred item.

The final spec reads 'lists mainly the starred items'. Commit 5082c20 weakened 'only' to 'mainly' after the go, with no recorded owner decision. The code and the AC-3 test still enforce 'only', but the item as written is vague and was edited without authority.
test 'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all give all items in id order.
test 'AC-5' checks both links on their views.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__; the code uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: Commit 5082c20 ('Follow-up edits') changed AC-3 from 'lists only the starred items' to 'lists mainly the starred items' after the go (2026-10-12). No decision in the spec records an owner call or date for this. It is a weakened acceptance item, and it contradicts the owner's request to 'show only the starred ones' and the 'Starred view' state row.
findings.fix: Revert AC-3 to 'only'. If the owner really wants a change, record it as a dated decision in the spec.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the spec's AC-3 was edited after the go (5082c20).
findings.fix: Revert the edit, or disclose it in the PR with the owner's decision.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none'. The traffic test's fake app was changed to key answers by path plus query. This is disclosed and not a loosening, so it is only a note.

lenses.note: A spec exists with a go; the code matches the intent, but the spec was edited after the go.

The tests assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. The traffic-config shell test covers both the query-accepting case and the space and # rejections.
The view lookup uses Object.hasOwn, so show=__proto__ cannot reach an inherited property. The SQL is static, with no user input.
The show value is only used as a lookup key. Titles are HTML-escaped. No injection found.
